correctness.rationale: The Harris--Tu product is independently matched to the dual Jacobi--Trudi determinant for the rectangular Schur class. For n=p^e, Lucas theorem makes that determinant strictly upper triangular modulo p, proving p divides every proper-rank degree. For n=p^e m with m>1 and p not dividing m, choosing corank c=p^e makes every factor in the localized product a p-adic unit by Lucas theorem, giving an explicit rank whose degree is not divisible by p. Because the determinant hypersurface has degree n, every common prime must divide n. These facts prove the stated iff classification without relying on finite computation.

value.rationale: The nested rank loci are the basic singular stratification of the determinant hypersurface and its deeper determinantal subvarieties. Classifying when all proper strata have degrees sharing a prime is a natural global arithmetic invariant of that entire stratification. The theorem gives a sharp prime-power dichotomy and, in the composite case, an explicit rank stratum that removes each candidate prime divisor.
